newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stock a touch higher in low volume.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stock a touch higher in low volume.

text.p: Shares on the Jordanian stock exchange rose slightly at start of weekly trade on Saturday in a day of narrow trading and low volume, dealers said.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.06 percent to 148.75 points at start of weekly trade in thin turnover worth 317,246 dinars ($448,087).
The market was again dominated by some speculative trade in Livestock and Poultry, which brokers say has been taken over by a single investor in recent weeks.
LIPO fell another 0.03 dinars to 0.63 dinars in a low 67,803 dinar turnover.
Aside from LIPO, two key industrial stock attracted some outside buying that helped score the day's highest price rises.

Blue-chip Jordan Cement Factories, from which Jordan wants to divest a 20 percent share in its 60 million dinar equity, rose 0.05 dinars to 3.35 dinars. Leading ready made garments manufacturer El-Zay rose a similar 0.05 dinars to 1.84 dinars
"The market lacks liquidity and the element of optimism that existed has evaporated...only those who are pinning hopes on foreign investors soon seem more optimistic," said one dealer.
Overall, 17 stocks closed unchanged on Saturday, 12 fell and only five rose in bearish sentiment caused by tight monetary policy and uncertainty over Middle East peace talks.
The market has remained in a wait-and-see mood since the recent flareup in violence in Palestinian self-rule areas.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange shed 0.04 percent to 80.78 points from 80.81 points, still 15.42 percent down from the same time last year.
